First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability using the complement:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =1-P(X\ge 4) \\  & =1-0.2119 \\  & =0.7881\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =0.7881 \\ P(Z\le \frac{4-1.8}{\sigma }) & =0.7881 \\ Φ(\frac{2.2}{\sigma }) & =0.7881 \\ \frac{2.2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7881)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.80)=0.7881\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7881)=0.80.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2.2}{\sigma } & =0.80 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2.2}{0.80} \\ \sigma  & =2.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2}={2.75}^{2}=7.56\end{aligned}
$$

to $2$ decimal places.

First, we express the given probability as

$$
P(|X|<2)=P(-2<X<2).
$$

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2<X<2) & =0.6826 \\ 2P(0<X<2) & =0.6826 \\ P(0<X<2) & =0.3413 \\ P(X<2)-P(X<0) & =0.3413 \\ P(X<2)-0.5 & =0.3413 \\ P(X<2) & =0.8413 \\ P(X\le 2) & =0.8413\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =0.8413 \\ P(Z\le \frac{2-0}{\sigma }) & =0.8413 \\ Φ(\frac{2}{\sigma }) & =0.8413 \\ \frac{2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8413)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.00)=0.8413\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.8413)=1.00.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sigma } & =1 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2}{1} \\ \sigma  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =(2)^{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(3,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(1<X<5)=0.3758,$ use the table to find  $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6808\,$ | $\,0.6844\,$ | $\,0.6879\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7157\,$ | $\,0.7190\,$ | $\,0.7224\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7486\,$ | $\,0.7517\,$ | $\,0.7549\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $1<X<5$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =3.$*

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that the given interval is symmetric about the mean:

$$
P(1<X<5)=P(3-2<X<3+2)
$$

So, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X<5) & =0.3758 \\ 2P(3<X<5) & =0.3758 \\ P(3<X<5) & =0.1879 \\ P(X<5)-P(X<3) & =0.1879 \\ P(X<5)-0.5 & =0.1879 \\ P(X<5) & =0.6879 \\ P(X\le 5) & =0.6879\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =0.6879 \\ P(Z\le \frac{5-3}{\sigma }) & =0.6879 \\ Φ(\frac{2}{\sigma }) & =0.6879 \\ \frac{2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.6879)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.49)=0.6879\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.6879)=0.49.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sigma } & =0.49 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2}{0.49} \\ \sigma  & ≈4.08\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(1,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-2<X<4)=0.6424,$ find ${\sigma }^{2},$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ | $\,0.8238\,$ |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-2<X<4$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =1.$*

${\sigma }^{2}≈$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2<X<4) & =0.6424 \\ 2P(1<X<4) & =0.6424 \\ P(1<X<4) & =0.3212 \\ P(X<4)-P(X<1) & =0.3212 \\ P(X<4)-0.5 & =0.3212 \\ P(X<4) & =0.8212 \\ P(X\le 4) & =0.8212\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =0.8212 \\ P(Z\le \frac{4-1}{\sigma }) & =0.8212 \\ Φ(\frac{3}{\sigma }) & =0.8212 \\ \frac{3}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8212)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.92)=0.8212\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.8212)=0.92.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sigma } & =0.92 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3}{0.92} \\ \sigma  & ≈3.260\,87.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2}=(3.260\,87)^{2}≈10.63\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
